note: The REGISTERED MODEL CATALOGUE for the deployed runtime (P-8 Phase 3).
Every model-specific fact lives here, as data: artifact + checksum, how a frame becomes a
tensor (`input`), how a tensor becomes detections (`outputFormat`), and the label space. The
runtime reads this and knows nothing about any model family — adding one is an entry here plus,
at most, one decoder in adapters/model_formats.py.
ONE MODEL, DELIBERATELY. The catalogue supports many and the runtime selects among them; this
deployment registers exactly one. A second family (SSD-MobileNetV1, tf-object-detection head)
was implemented and MEASURED through this same unchanged runtime during P-8 Phase 3, which is
the evidence that the seam is real — and then removed, because an unexercised decoder in a
serving container is surface without a customer. Architect's direction: one production-quality
path before breadth.
LICENSING IS A SELECTION CRITERION. The obvious choice (Ultralytics YOLOv8/v11) is AGPL-3.0,
which is not usable in a commercial product without a paid licence. YOLOX is Apache-2.0.
ONE LABEL CONVENTION: `labels` is indexed by the class id the model emits. A model with a
1-based label map therefore carries an empty placeholder at index 0, and no code rebases ids.
Artifacts are NOT committed. They are fetched by fetch_models.py at image build time and
verified against `sha256` here — and verified AGAIN at process start, so 'the artifact is
present' and 'the artifact we registered is present' are different questions with the same
answer.
TWO DETECTORS ARE REGISTERED AND ONE IS NOT, FOR REASONS WORTH READING (P-10 A2).
rtdetr-r18vd is `disabled`: a real, checksum-pinned artifact this deployment does not run. It was
exported by ai/mlops/export_rtdetr_onnx.py from the authors' Apache-2.0 PyTorch weights, because
the only ready-made ONNX conversion of it declares no licence of its own. `source` is therefore
null — the artifact is produced, not downloaded — and fetch_models.py skips disabled entries so a
build never fails over a model nobody enabled.
yolo11 has a DECODER but NO CATALOGUE ENTRY, deliberately. Ultralytics YOLO11 is AGPL-3.0, whose
section 13 obliges anyone serving it over a network to offer the complete corresponding source of
the combined work to its users — which a commercial multi-tenant deployment cannot do. VIP ships
neither the weights nor a way to fetch them. An entry is not written because its most important
field cannot be filled honestly: we have never obtained the artifact, so we do not know its
sha256, and inventing one would defeat the only check that makes this catalogue worth having.
A licensee supplies the artifact and adds the entry; MODEL_PLUGIN_GUIDE.md records its shape.
